statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer greater than 1. For which real numbers $x$ is \\[\\lfloor nx \\rfloor - \\sum_{k=1}^{n} \\frac{\\lfloor kx \\rfloor}{k}\\] maximal, and what is the maximal value that this expression can take?

domain_restrictions: n is an integer with n > 1
k is an integer index with 1 <= k <= n inside the sum
x ranges over all real numbers
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: Fix any integer n with n > 1. Define f_n(x) = floor(n x) - sum from k=1 to n of (floor(k x) divided by k). Determine the real number(s) x where f_n(x) attains its maximum over all real x, and give the corresponding maximum value.
quantifier_order: for each integer n with n > 1
choose real x to maximize the expression over all real x

variables.name: x
variables.role: optimization variable (argument of floors and sum)

witness_dependencies: the maximizing real number(s) x* (or argmax set) may depend on n
the maximal value M may depend on n
